Evaluate background and triggering intensity on a spatial grid over time

Source: R/background_trigger_grid.R
background_trigger_grid.Rd

Computes, for each day in the study period (or a user-supplied set of days), the background intensity \(\mu(s,t)\) and the triggering intensity \(A \cdot g(t) \cdot f(s)\) on a regular spatial grid covering city. This is the building block behind exceedance-set and persistence analyses: it turns a fitted semihawkes_fit object into daily snapshots of both intensity components that can later be aggregated over periods (yearly, semestral, quarterly, ...) via integrate_intensity_period().

Usage

background_trigger_grid(
  fit,
  city,
  cell_size = 150,
  days = NULL,
  t.lag = 90,
  s.lag = NULL,
  nprocs = 1
)

Arguments

fit

A semihawkes_fit object (or equivalently-shaped list) with $events, $mu, $A, $trend, $weekly, $monthly, $background, $temporal_trigger, $spatial_trigger.

city

An sf polygon giving the study region. Used both to build the evaluation grid (from its bounding box) and to mask grid cells outside the region (via spatstat.geom::inside.owin()).

cell_size

Grid spacing, in the same spatial units as city (e.g. metres for UTM data). Default 150.

days

Integer vector of days-since-start_date at which to evaluate the intensity. Defaults to 0:TT, where TT <- max(fit$events$events$days) + 1.

t.lag

Only triggering events within this many days before t contribute (events further in the past are dropped for speed, on the assumption their contribution has decayed to ~0). Default 90.

s.lag

Only triggering events within this spatial distance of the grid's bounding box contribute. The default, NULL, uses the reach of the fitted spatial triggering kernel, beyond which its contribution is zero.

nprocs

Number of parallel workers, via foreach/doParallel. nprocs = 1 (default) runs sequentially with no cluster overhead. With more, the workers are stopped on exit and the sequential foreach backend is registered in their place.

Value

A list with:

days

the days at which intensity was evaluated (matches the days argument).

x, y

grid coordinate vectors.

inside

logical vector, TRUE for grid cells inside city.

snapshots

a list (one element per day) of lists with $bg and $tr, each a length(x) by length(y) matrix of intensity values. Cells outside city are 0.

Details

Unlike background_intensity() and em_step(), which evaluate the model only at observed event locations (for likelihood/EM purposes), this function evaluates it on an arbitrary regular grid, independent of the grid resolution background_spatial() used internally during fitting. You choose the grid resolution via cell_size.

fit$background$fun, fit$trend$fun, fit$weekly$fun, fit$monthly$fun, fit$temporal_trigger$fun and fit$spatial_trigger$fun are assumed to be the final, converged fit – i.e. fit is the result of a completed fit_semihawkes() run (or the last em_step() in a manual loop), not an initial Loop-0 guess.

Examples

# \donttest{
# A quick fit to one year of the bundled simulated data: a coarse grid, a
# coarse triggering-kernel grid and two EM iterations keep it to a few
# seconds. Real analyses need finer settings and more iterations.
cache_dir <- tempfile("spHawkes_marks_")
fit <- fit_semihawkes(
  sim_events, sim_region,
  date_col  = "date",
  end_date  = "2022-01-01",
  cell_size = 1000,
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  trigger_spatial_args = list(x_range = 2000, x_step = 250),
  trigger_window_dist  = 2000,
  n_iter  = 2,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed    = 1
)
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
# Evaluate on a handful of days rather than the whole study window
grid <- background_trigger_grid(fit, sim_region, cell_size = 500,
                                days = c(0, 100, 200))
length(grid$snapshots)
#> [1] 3
dim(grid$snapshots[[1]]$bg)
#> [1] 17 17
# }
